title: Refuse a reservation the session store can't trust

blocks.text: The web tier keeps a guest's `Reservation` in the session, and the session store writes sessions out as serialized objects and reads them back on whichever node takes the next request. Since last month's release the price page sometimes shows a stay for 0 nights or for 9 guests, values the constructor has always refused. The session store logs a stream it can't read as an `IOException` and starts a fresh session; anything else it lets through to the error page.

Finish `readObject` in `src/main/java/practice/Reservation.java`, so that a reservation read back from a stream holds to the same rules as one built with the constructor, and a stream that breaks them reaches the session store as a stream it can't read.

cases.says: a valid reservation written to a stream and read back has the same room, guests and nights
a stream whose guests or nights the constructor would refuse is refused, and no reservation comes back
the refusal reaches the caller as an IOException, the way a stream that can't be read does

origin.section: Deserialization Builds the Object Without Your Constructor, So readObject Checks Again

concepts: Deserializing a Serializable class runs only the no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass, so readObject repeats the constructor's checks after defaultReadObject and throws InvalidObjectException.
